      New Game

      You are creating a multiplayer game. Your empire name and race below are yours; the other players choose theirs when they join. Set the player spots and AI opponents under Opponents, and privacy and custom races under Advanced Options.
      Off: the original game. On: every Game+ feature is part of this game (new options appear in Advanced Options). It cannot be changed after the galaxy is built.
      You only watch: every empire is an AI. Each year runs in steps: every AI in turn chooses its orders (you see them, then a wait), the year is played out, and a Year-End Summary is shown (another wait). Continue skips a wait. If the steps finish early, the summary stays up until the Minimum Time per Year has passed. Set the AI empires up under AI Opponents (at least 2). They play until one meets the Victory Conditions or is the last empire left. The simulation runs only while this page is open, and it is not saved. Tip: for a game that always ends, turn on Highest Score after a number of years in Victory Conditions.

      AI Opponents

      Add or remove AI opponents and set each one's empire name, race and intelligence level. Every opponent starts with a pre-generated empire name you can change. Choose Random for a race or intelligence level and the game picks one when the galaxy is created. Your saved custom races are listed under Custom Races in each race menu.

      Research

      Technology Tree
      Research Known
      Research Queue (plan up to 100 years ahead)
      Line up fields in order, each for a number of years. While the queue runs it decides the research field each year and replaces the Active Research Field choice above. If a field reaches its maximum before its years are up, the queue moves on to the next entry by itself. When the queue is empty the Active Research Field simply carries on.
      Explanation

      Paying for research. Research is paid in Resources. The Research Allocation on the Economy screen sends that share of your empire's yearly Resources to research, and every Resource your planets' production queues leave unused that year goes to research too. It all flows into the Active Research Field (or the field the Research Queue picks). With the Generalized Research trait half goes to the current field and 15% to each of the six fields.

      Levels and costs. Each of the six fields runs from level 0 to 26. When a field collects enough Resources it gains a level, and any extra carries over. Level costs grow quickly (50, 80, 130, 210, 340, 550 and so on), and every level costs 10 Resources more for each level you already hold in all six fields together, so research gets dearer as your empire advances. Slower Tech Advances doubles all costs, and a custom race can pay 75% extra or 50% less in chosen fields. The numbers above always show your real cost.

      What levels give you. New levels unlock parts, hulls and installations: Energy for shields and power, Weapons for beams, torpedoes and bombs, Propulsion for engines, stargates and mass drivers, Construction for hulls and armor, Electronics for scanners, computers and cloaks, Biotechnology for terraforming and planetary scanners. Levels above an item's requirement also make it cheaper to build (miniaturization). Surviving a battle against ships with better technology gives up to a 50% chance to learn a level in a field where the enemy was ahead.

      Technology Tree. Pick one of the six field cards to see its levels in four tiers, Early to Ultimate. Green levels are reached and the gold one is next. Click a level to see what it unlocks; ??? marks technology you have not discovered yet. Research this now makes the shown field the active one.

      Research Queue. Plan up to 100 years ahead: add fields for a number of years, or until they reach a level (those entries do not count toward the 100). While the queue runs it chooses the field each year; when a field maxes out early it moves on, and when the queue ends the last field carries on.

      Economic Status:

      Explanation
      Resources are your industrial labor: they come from colonists and operating factories. Ore (Ironium, Boranium, Germanium) is the raw matter dug up by mines. Everything you build needs both. Split your Resources between research and planetary manufacturing; unspent manufacturing Resources are lost. Total must equal 100%.

      ⚙ Advanced Options

      Tick any option to add it to this game. These settings are locked in when you press Create Galaxy and are saved with the game.
      Multiplayer Options
      4 to 64 characters. Give it to the players you want; anyone you invite by email or username joins without it.
      Off: every empire uses one of the six built-in races. On: custom races from the Race Wizard may be played, by these rules:
      hours minutes
      Any amount from 1 minute to 30 days, in hours and minutes. When a player has had the turn for longer than this, any other player can skip it. The skipped empire follows its standing orders for that turn. Unticked means no limit.
      Off (the default): nobody can be added once the galaxy is built. On: the host gets an Invite to Game button in Settings and can bring new players into the running game.
      Game Options

      ✉ Invite to Game

      Invite someone into this game while it is running. They get an email with a link; after they sign in they create their empire and start on a random uninhabited planet.

      🎨 Empire Color

      Pick a new color for your empire. Only colors that no other empire holds are listed. Everyone sees the change within a few seconds.

      Join Game

      Only colors no other empire has are listed.

      🧬 Custom Races

      Design your own races with the Race Wizard. Saved races appear under Custom Races in Choose Race and in every AI opponent's race list. They are kept in this browser and copied into every saved game that uses them.

      🏆 Victory Conditions

      Tick the conditions that can win the game and set their values. Owning 60% of all planets is ticked to start with. With nothing ticked the game never ends on its own. Every empire, AI included, is judged by the same rules.
      Own at least % of all planets (10 to 100)
      Reach level (1 to 26) in of the 6 fields (1 to 6)
      Score of at least (1,000 to 1,000,000)
      Have a score at least % higher than the second place empire (1 to 1,000)
      Own at least capital ships (2 to 1,000)
      Have the highest score after years (10 to 1,000,000)
      A winner must meet of the above criteria to win
      At least years must pass before a winner is declared (10 to 1,000,000)

      Autobuild Rules

      Explanation
      When a planet's build queue runs empty, the game reads this list from the top. The first rule that applies adds an item to the queue and the planet carries on building in the same turn. A rule is skipped if the planet cannot pay the Ore for one unit, so a planet never queues something it cannot build. Rules apply to every planet of your empire.

      🤝 Diplomacy

      Explanation
      Everyone starts neutral. Neutral: ask for an alliance or declare war. Allied: break the alliance (both become neutral) or declare war. At War: request a stand down (both become neutral if accepted). Orders happen when the year is played out; a war starts the year after. Only empires at war fight each other.

      💣 Minefields

      How minefields are shown
      Your fields are blue, friends' yellow, neutral and enemy fields red. You see another empire's field when its center is inside your planet-penetrating scanner range, when one of your fleets is inside it, or when you have hit it before and its center is inside your normal scanner range. Press Go on a row to move the star map to that field's center.

      Files for Claude
      Download the whole database as one SQL file (tables, security rules, functions, triggers and permissions, no player data) and the notify.ts email function, so you can attach them in chat when Claude needs them.
      Minimum Game Version
      Players whose page is older than this version cannot send turns, start games or save multiplayer galaxies (the server refuses them and they are told to reload). Single player is never affected. Needs script 42_min_version.sql.
      Current: ?
      Note: notify.ts is the copy built into the game, not necessarily the code deployed in Supabase (Supabase does not let a function hand out its own file). To get the exact deployed code, copy it from the Supabase dashboard under Edge Functions, notify, Code.
      Administrators
      Inactive Accounts
      Accounts with no sign in for a year get a warning email, and are deleted a month later if they still have not signed in. Admins are never deleted. The server checks this by itself (at most every 6 hours, whenever the email function runs); these buttons let you look or run it now.
